sources.entry: StockDock - Menu bar app for real-time stocks, ETFs, crypto and portfolio P&L. Privacy-first, no account, multi-currency. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/simonsruggi/StockDock) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: StockDock is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that shows real-time prices and portfolio P&L for stocks, ETFs, indices, crypto and forex.
summary.what_it_does: It lives in the macOS menu bar and displays watchlist prices, daily changes and portfolio profit and loss, using Yahoo Finance WebSocket and REST endpoints. Users can search symbols, company names or ISINs, and build multiple portfolios with holdings, average cost and purchase dates, with multi-currency conversion using historical rates on cost basis. It offers one-shot price alerts, per-portfolio notifications, and optional Discord or Slack webhook mirroring. A desktop window, optional long/short and leverage math, optional overnight and weekend prices from Hyperliquid, and JSON export/import of portfolios are also included. The README states that all data is stored locally in a data.json file and that there is no account or telemetry.
use_cases: track stock prices from the macOS menu bar
monitor portfolio profit and loss in multiple currencies
set price alerts on stocks or crypto
get Discord or Slack notifications for portfolio moves
watch ETFs and market indices in one place
export and import portfolio data as JSON
stack: Yahoo Finance WebSocket and REST API
notable: Menu bar P&L display with selectable options such as best/worst stock and total value
Optional desktop window with watchlist, portfolios, charts and news
Multi-currency portfolios with historical exchange rates applied to cost basis
Price alerts and portfolio notifications with Discord or Slack webhook support
Universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel, auto-updates via Sparkle
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later and Xcode 15+ to build from source
Prices may be delayed or inaccurate and the README says it is not investment advice
Overnight and weekend prices from Hyperliquid are perpetual futures prices, not official exchange quotes
keywords: see my stock gains in menu bar
